title: Unsafe Channel Protocol Coupling
pattern: Two threads communicate via raw channels without a compiler-enforced state machine or structural protocol, relying on implicit, manual synchronization order.
why_bad: If one thread deviates from the expected message sequence (e.g., sending two messages instead of one), the receiving thread will mismatch types or hang forever in a deadlock.
detection: The use of untyped channels or simple channels passing primitive types in complex bidirectional communication flows.
counterexample: Unidirectional pipeline threads where data flows strictly in one direction from producer to consumer.
fix:
Define structural protocol enums that represent exact protocol phases, or enforce communication states using Rust's type-state system.
```rust
enum Protocol {
    Handshake(String),
    Command(u32),
    Terminate,
}
```
source: Edwin Brady, *Type-driven Development with Idris* (2017), Chapter 15 ("Problems with channels: type errors and blocking").
